answer: Block sybil farms stamping thousands of keys. Each identity etches its key on a copper strip, hung in the zephyr tunnel for one hour; airflow presses ferrous dust into the grooves, and auditors weigh the dust against its chart. Hung uninterrupted, it serves one identity only. Faking N accounts takes N strips, N slots and N parallel hours, 24x one honest cost; a borrowed strip fails, dust matching another key. Honest users pay one strip, one hour.
